title: The Craftsman, February 1915
lede: Gustav Stickley’s magazine of the American movement opens its issue with a heavy masthead between two joiner’s-compass devices and a woodcut initial.
summary: Heavy condensed capitals between two compass devices, a woodcut initial, and dense old-style text. The Craftsman, 1915.

source.label: Internet Archive: The Craftsman 1915-02, Vol. 27, Issue 5

creator.name: Gustav Stickley (publisher); The Craftsman Publishing Co.

evidence.note: Inspected page 459, the first text page of the issue, in the Internet Archive microfilm scan (1468 × 2006 px, greyscale), saved only in a scratch folder. The scan is black and white, so colour cannot be judged. The printed cover, on [Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:The_Craftsman_vol._XXVII_no._5,_Feb._1915_cover.jpg), could not be downloaded because of repeated HTTP 429 rate limits and was not inspected.

styles.note: Partial fit: the American branch. Heavy capitals, a device, and a woodcut initial over dense text, without the British pattern.

context: Stickley founded The Craftsman in October 1901 to promote the American Arts and Crafts movement; the first issue’s cover story was on William Morris. The last issue appeared in December 1916. [Wikipedia: The Craftsman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Craftsman_(magazine)).

This issue is Volume XXVII, Number 5, February 1915, published by the Craftsman Publishing Co.; its opening article is “My People” by Robert Henri. [Internet Archive](https://archive.org/details/sim_craftsman-an-illustrated-monthly-magazine_1915-02_27_5).
observed: “THE CRAFTSMAN” runs across the top in heavy, condensed, slightly irregular capitals.
A black device stands at each end of the masthead: a joiner’s compass shape with the words “Als ik kan” in a small panel.
Under it, a line of small bold capitals gives the publisher, volume, date, and number.
The article title “MY PEOPLE:” BY ROBERT HENRI is in bold capitals; an editor’s note follows in smaller type.
A square black woodcut initial T, with a small landscape inside it, opens the text.
The text is a single wide column of dark old-style serif with tight spacing and narrow margins.
interpretation: The page shares the British private-press habits of a device, a woodcut initial, and a dark text block, but its masthead lettering is a condensed display face, not a blackletter or Venetian roman. That is typical of the American branch, which the style record treats as related.
The Dutch motto “Als ik kan” (“as I can”) in the devices states the craft ideal in the masthead itself. Its history was not checked for this record.
borrow: Frame a masthead between two matching square devices.
Open an article with a square woodcut-style initial that holds a small picture.

rights.statement: The issue was published in the United States in 1915 and is in the public domain there. The Internet Archive microfilm scan carries no rights statement, so no image is stored.
